msContents.summary: [p]"Altissimus liber et profundus ubi continentur multa segreta [sic] chimica, alchimica et de Lapide Philosophico. G[iuseppe] D[e] M[ogliettis] A[ssisio]."[/p][p] The text mainly written about 1550 by an unnamed compiler, but with added receipts and notes by G. de Mogliettis: in Latin and Italian.[/p][p]Ms 563/10 (fols. 132r-169r) is apparently copied from [i]Rosarium philosophorum secunda pars alchimiae de lapide philosophico vero modo praeparando, continens exactam eius scientiae progressionem[/i] (Madrid: Offic. Cyriaci Jacobi, 1550), fol. D2v ff. [/p][p]On fol. 231 is a rough pen-drawing of the 'Arbor alchemica'. [/p][p]The t.p. (second leaf) is surrounded by a historiated border in four panels, containing pen-drawings, tinted in red, of alchemical apparatus, etc. It is surmounted by an unidentified heraldic shield: on a fess, three bulls' heads. [/p][p]The 12 preliminary leaves, and from fol. 234 to the end, are holograph by G. de Mogliettis: on the fifth leaf is the date 1659, and on the seventh 'G.M.D.A. 1658'.[/p] [li]Sedacerius, G. Opus totius artis alchimiae. Fol. 1 Incipit opus totius Artis Alchimie Edita a fratre Gulielmo / Sedaceriensi ordinis fratrum Beate Marie et Monte Carmeli / existendo in exilio Sui sacri Ordinis electa de Medicinis / verissimis approbatorum philosophorum et antiquorum. / Omne Donum datum optimum ... 83v ...et sic terminatur opus in capitulo de galina. / Finis operis fratris ioannis [sic] Sedacine [sic] ordinis / Carmelitarum. laus Deo et Virginis / eius Matris Marie.[/li][li][Sedacerius G. ?]. De multiplicatione. Fol. 84 Sequitur modus quomodo multiplicantur Medicine supra dicte / in virtute et potentia. / Quando perfeceris dictas medicinas ... 87v ...postea in infinitum in quantitate per proiec / tionem, et hec de Multiplicatione dicta sufficiant. / Finis laus Deo per infinita seculi.[/li][li][Anon.]. De lapide philosophico: in Italian verse. Fol. 87v, line 11 Qual scientia e si profunda / O qual arte si ingeniosa / ... 88 Di essa famo cum gran cura / Noi imitiamo la natura.[/li][li]Pantheo, G.A. Voarchadumia. Extract: in Latin. Fol. 88v Dedicatio operis Andree Griti... 114 ... Nisi soluatur in / primam Materiam, i.e. in Aquam sulphuris.[/li][li]Arnoldus de Villanova. De sanguine humano (etc.). Fol. 114v Incipit tractatus primus et ultimus in scientie occulte philosophia. / Interrogationibus uestris quas nobis remitto. 117v ...probatum est per me et certum.[/li][li][Anon.] De salibus, etc.. Fol. 117v-123v.[/li][li][Bonaventura de Iseo]. Alchemical terms: in Latin. Fol. 123v Solutio est uno modo aliquid durum sic exercitare ... 125v ...et sic potest / in tali statu perseuerare. Laus Deo semper. extracta de libro / Compostelle.[/li][li]Mappae Clavicula. Extracts. Fol. 125v Incipit liber Mappe Alchel philosophi / Incipit in nomine domini Alpha et O... 131v ...et exinde / mercedem reperies. Laus deo patri et fillio [sic] / et spiritui sancto per infinita / secula. amen.[/li][li]Extracts from the works of Hermes Trismegistus, Geber, and other alchemical writers. Ff. 132-169 in Latin.[/li][li]Pseudo-Democritus. Secretum naturae. Fol. 169v: Democritus philosophus. / Oportet te ut in primo negotio dissoluas corpora... 172 ... thesaurus incomparabilis et preciosissimus quem / habentibus Deus in sua mente recordat ne incipientibus patefiat. amen / dicat omnis viuens. Laus deo per infinita secula. amen. ¶ This text is apparently copied from Rosarium philosophorum secunda pars alchimiae de lapide philosophico vero modo praeparando, continens exactam eius scientiae progressionem (Madrid: Offic. Cyriaci Jacobi, 1550), fol. D2v ff.[/li][li]Bonus, P. Excerpta from his 'Pretiosa margarita novella'. Ff. 172v-185.[/li][li]Miscellaneous chemical and alchemical receipts, with a few medical receipts. Fol. 186-211 in Latin and Italian.[/li][li]Khalid ibn Jazid. Liber trium verborum. Fol. 211v Liber trium verborum Kalid acutissimi. / Lapis iste de quo fit hoc opus... 214, line 19 de / hoc suo tanto et suo sancto dono. Amen. fiat. fiat. / Libri trium verborum Kallid Rachaidibi philosophi finis.[/li][li]Avicenna. De quatuor speciebus corporum mineralium. Fol. 214, line 21 Corpora mineralia in quatuor species diuiduntur... 215v, line 7 ...sed / accidunt ei res extranee.[/li][li](Khalid ibn Jazid). De materia lapidis fragmenta. Fol. 215v, line 9 Rachaidbi veradiani rodiani et Kanidis philosophi Regis persarum de Materia / philosophici lapidis accutissime colloquentium fragmenta. / Dixit Rachiadibi filius Retheididi philosophus Regis persarum et principis / Romanorum. Sperma lapidis est frigidum ... 217v, line 23 ...quod est color phaulet ad tingendum in solem obrizum.[/li][li]Sabeo F. Alchemical poem. Fol. 217v, line 24 Faustus Sabaeus ad lectorem. / Femina, vir, neutrum, sibimet pater, atque creatrix, / Et se concipiens se quoque parturiens, / ... 218, line 14 Si capitur trepidus, hac ratione latet.[/li][li]Rhazes, (?). Epistola. Line 15 Autoris philosophici ignoti lapidis secreta Metaphorice describentis opusculum. / Exemplum scientiae nostrae (senex supra mortem [sic for 'montem'])... 219, line 19 ...ex pietate, et detexi cunctis per Deum gentium.[/li][li]Alchemical, chemical and medical receipts and notes. Fol. 219, line 20-233 in Latin and Italian.[/li][li]Prayers and charms in Italian against natural disasters, diseases, etc. by G. de Mogliettis. Fol. 234-end.[/li]

msItem.filiation: On fol. 172 is a reference to the 'De alchimia opuscula complura' published by C. Jacobus at Frankfort in 1550. No. 17 is also doubtfully attributed to Arnoldus de Villanova ('Flores lilii') in Thorndike 'Catalogue of Incipits', col. 256, also in his 'History of Magic and Experimental Science' Vol. III, pp. 62, 63, 660, 661: Mrs. Singer's 'Catalogue of Alchemical MSS., No. 120, assigns it to Rhazes. Fol. 230v contains the explanatory text, and Fol. 231 the Diagram of an 'Alchemical Tree', by the 16th cent. compiler. The text begins: 'Ista est arbor composita de principiis Alphabeti et est composita ad finem quod magis breuiter Artista / huius artis possit venire ad finem desideratum...'. In the diagram itself: 'A significat hominem seu primum principium quod est chaos': it ends: 'z [significat] euacuationem'. On the first leaf a 17th cent. hand has written 'Questo libro e stato messo in questa libreria dal Sig. Canonico Teologo Francesco Piervesani in luogo di deposito che poi lo riprendera'. Written
